newsitem.title: PERU: Commandos executed Peruvian rebels, hostages say.
newsitem.headline: Commandos executed Peruvian rebels, hostages say.

text.p: Peruvian commandos executed one Marxist guerrilla and killed others who had surrendered during the assault on the Japanese ambassador's residence to free 72 VIPs, former hostages and news media reports said on Thursday.

One rebel was captured alive, taken away and shot, a freed hostage told Japan's Asahi news service. "I realised that the arrested rebel was killed when I heard a report that all 14 rebel members died in the raid," the unnamed former hostage said after Tuesday's dramatic raid.

Two teenage girls among the guerrillas were clearly heard giving themselves up as troops stormed the mansion from tunnels and holes blasted through the floor and walls, the newspaper La Republica reported.
"We surrender! We surrender!" the girls shouted, according to an intelligence agent who monitored the raid through listening devices, the paper said.
Many of the rebels were killed on the lower floor of the house when commandos blew up their indoor soccer game.

Agriculture Minister Rodolfo Munante said one who tried to surrender was machine-gunned by the elite army troops. "One rebel surrendered in the room where the judges where ... he told the judges he surrendered, but then (a soldier) entered and machine-gunned (the rebels) in the room," Munante told the Spanish-language news channel CBS/Telenoticias.
Military sources said the commando units were under orders to take no prisoners and each rebel was given a final "coup de grace" shot in the forehead to make sure they were dead.

A Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) member in Lima told Reuters shortly after Tuesday's assault that four of the younger rebels had been shot by troops despite making it clear they wanted to surrender. "They were the four youngest. They were in a room on their own. They gave up out of fear," said the rebel, who heard the surrender on a short-wave radio.
One hostage and two soldiers died in the assault, which rescued 71 VIPs after 126 days in captivity.
